clue.text: Sound artist out

indicators.note: letters that are out of place have been knocked from their proper order

blocks.note: the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A painter has left the room, or a musician's tone is off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a verb or noise, but it is the definition: a sound is a narrow sea channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound and a strait are both geographical terms for a narrow stretch of water linking two larger seas.

clue.text: Impractical figure out to cover cooking vessel

blocks.note: to crack a code is to figure it out
a pot is a pan for cooking

explanation.surface: Someone trying to work out how to fit a lid on a pan.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, the first piece covering the second means it sits on top of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackpot as an adjective describes schemes or ideas that are eccentric and unworkable.

clue.text: Takeaway food put in large vessel for horse

indicators.note: one item is placed inside another, so these letters go within the vessel

blocks.note: a common takeaway dish
an ocean liner is a big ship

explanation.surface: Someone loading a pizza into a big container to feed a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a pot or dish to hold the food, but here it is a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lipizzaner is a white breed of horse famous at Vienna's Spanish Riding School.

clue.text: Marsupial, one breaking ring on bird

indicators.note: something breaking into a sequence forces its way between its parts

blocks.note: a band is a ring, as of metal
Roman numeral for one
the coot is a water bird

explanation.surface: An Australian animal is breaking a ring attached to a bird's leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring on bird' sets the two outer pieces side by side, and the one breaks into the join between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The bandicoot is a small pouched mammal of Australia and New Guinea, so it is a marsupial.

clue.text: Very, very unremarkable

blocks.note: so means very, as in so tired
the same word again

explanation.surface: Someone stressing how dull something was.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so is an informal way of describing something mediocre or merely average.

clue.text: Quiet moment for routine

blocks.note: the hushing sound asking for quiet
a tick is a moment, as in just a tick

explanation.surface: A short silence set aside as part of a daily schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: A tick meaning a moment is British informal usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A shtick is a comedian's or performer's characteristic act, their familiar routine.

clue.text: Animal skirting round trap in dark

definitions.note: adjective for a dark-haired person; the answer is usually a noun

indicators.note: to skirt round something is to go about its edges, enclosing it

blocks.note: a brute is a beast
a net traps fish or game

explanation.surface: A creature edges around a snare at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark' as the definition is fair because a brunette is described by her dark hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A brunette has dark brown hair, so the word describes someone of dark colouring.

clue.text: Piece of cake tethering stray dog

indicators.note: tethering holds something fast, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: one layer of a wedding cake is a tier
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: A slice of cake used to keep a wandering dog tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of cake' tempts as the idiom for something easy, but it is one layer of a tiered cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a small breed of dog originally bred to hunt burrowing animals.

clue.text: Payment cut

blocks.note: first meaning: money paid for use of property
second meaning: torn or split, as a past participle

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the old past participle of rend, meaning torn apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a tenant's regular charge and also means torn, as in a rent garment.

clue.text: Extra rioting on earth

indicators.note: a rioting crowd is in disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A headline about yet more civil unrest around the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means one more, an additional one, so it fits extra as an adjective.

clue.text: A gross I counted, sold

indicators.note: gross suggests something crude and mangled, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trader tallying a gross, 144 items, before they went.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gross' looks like the number 144 here, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Auctioned means sold by public bidding to the highest offer, a particular kind of sale.

clue.text: Hunter of rhino regularly ending in prison

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is taken
the ending of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters of these two words
its final letter

explanation.surface: A poacher of rhinos who ends up behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunter of rhino' reads as one phrase, but 'of' belongs to the letter selection.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is the great hunter of Greek myth, and the constellation named after him.

clue.text: Stone to kill, lobbed over

indicators.note: something lobbed over is flipped end to end, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
to zap is to kill, in slang

explanation.surface: Someone hurling a rock with intent to kill.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the word for kill turns round, after TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Topaz is a gemstone, a precious stone usually yellow or golden.

clue.text: Jumpy little thing in game of ins and outs?

blocks.note: first meaning: a small leaping insect
second meaning: a bat-and-ball game where batsmen are in and then out

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is a bat-and-ball sport in which each side takes turns batting, so players go in and are given out.
explanation.definitionFit: The insect hops about chirping, and the sport is played with sides batting in turn until dismissed.

clue.text: Business proceedings under Asian runner

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece under another is written below it, so the proceedings come second

blocks.note: a runner is a river; the Indus flows through Pakistan
court proceedings

explanation.surface: Commercial litigation beneath an Asian athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one piece under another comes after it. A runner is crossword shorthand for a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrial relates to industry, meaning business and manufacturing, as in industrial dispute.

clue.text: Shuffle around selection of lowest parts?

blocks.note: the rear is the bottom or behind
a range is a selection, as of goods

explanation.surface: A query about moving the bottom tier of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the reverse order to the clue: lowest parts first, then the selection of them.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange things is to move them into a different order, which is what shuffling around does.

clue.text: Political understanding required, as nation re-elected maverick?

indicators.note: a maverick refuses to stay in line, so the letters break their order

blocks.note: the fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A country votes back an unorthodox leader and needs an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maverick' seems to describe the re-elected politician, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Entente Cordiale was the 1904 Anglo-French agreement, and the phrase now means any friendly diplomatic accord.

clue.text: Dreamer is set to travel around peak

indicators.note: letters set to travel move about, landing in a new order
around means encircling, so the rearranged letters go about the next piece

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
the peak of a cap, or a cap as the top of something

explanation.surface: A daydreamer planning a trip around a mountain summit.
explanation.walkthrough: CAP sits inside the rearranged letters after the first two.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapist is someone who retreats from reality into fantasy, a dreamer.

clue.text: A message about motorway showed goodwill

definitions.note: verb phrase; the answer is an adjective, friendly

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the message goes round the road

blocks.note: taken as written
a cable is a telegram
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A text sent from the motorway signalled friendliness.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main motorway from London to Leeds, written with I for 1. A cable is an old word for a telegram.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means friendly and showing goodwill, so it describes behaviour that showed goodwill, though as an adjective.

clue.text: Provider of food feeding endless tea to guardian

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped
feeding goes into something, so these letters go inside the other piece

blocks.note: the word with its last letter cut
a carer looks after someone

explanation.surface: A cook keeps feeding cups of tea to a care worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer supplies food and drink for events, a professional provider of meals.

clue.text: One in temple raised on an island off the Chinese mainland

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means lifted upward, so the word reads bottom to top
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia
Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worshipper elevated in a shrine on an offshore island.
explanation.walkthrough: The temple word turns upward, takes I inside, and sits on AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiwan is the large island across the strait from mainland China.

clue.text: Change dress

blocks.note: first meaning: to move or alter
second meaning: a loose straight dress

explanation.walkthrough: 'Change dress' reads as a single instruction to get changed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for altering position and a noun for a simple straight-cut dress.

clue.text: Sun seemingly in old money?

blocks.note: first meaning: the sun appears to brown the skin
second meaning: a pre-decimal British coin

explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was the slang name for the old British sixpence coin. 'In old money' looks like an idiom for old-fashioned terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that tans skin is a tanner, which the sun appears to be; and the sixpence carried the same nickname.

clue.text: Great film inferior to theatre, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last thing, here the final letter

blocks.note: its final letter
pic is short for picture, a film

explanation.surface: A judgement that a fine movie still falls short of live stage drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great film' reads as one phrase, but only 'Great' is the definition. In a down clue, inferior to means placed below.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic as an informal adjective means great or impressive, as in an epic win.

clue.text: Colour isn't on front of package

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: its first letter
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A complaint that the box has no colour printed on it.
explanation.walkthrough: One piece on another in an across clue may come after it; here the P leads.
explanation.definitionFit: To colour something is to apply pigment to it, which is what to paint means.

clue.text: Slight guess, inconclusive

indicators.note: without a conclusion means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: to think is to suppose or guess

explanation.surface: A tentative hunch that settles nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Slight and thin both describe something of little substance or a slender build.

clue.text: Relate to a forward in agony

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
pert means cheeky or forward
pain is agony

explanation.surface: A link to a footballer in agony after a tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' suggests a football player, but it is an adjective meaning cheeky or bold.
explanation.definitionFit: To appertain to something is to belong or relate to it, a formal synonym.

clue.text: By the sound of it, roof closing

indicators.note: this phrase asks the solver to judge by how a word is spoken

blocks.note: the ceiling is the roof of a room

explanation.surface: A builder judging by the noise whether the roof is closing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sealing something means closing it up tightly, as with an envelope.

clue.text: Idiot put fish with pork pie!

blocks.note: the char is a trout-like fish
rhyming slang: pork pie means lie

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone serving fish with a pork pie.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for lie, often shortened to porky.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlie is British informal for a fool, as in a proper charlie.
